evals.prompt: Add ingestion support for a new licensed runway-photo source per P12-T05: fetch -> validate -> hash dedup -> publish draft, idempotent and retryable.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks that a rights-basis record exists for the source (or stops if it does not), implements the fetch as a ContentSourcePort adapter bound in apps/api/src/platform/ rather than a direct HTTP call inside fashion-intel's domain code, writes content_items through the draft state, and makes the job idempotent (per-source singletonKey / dedup hash) so re-runs do not duplicate items. It reports which validation commands it ran. Because pg-boss and the outbox relay are not built (P02-T08 NOT_STARTED) and fashion-intel is a P02 skeleton, the agent reports what is missing and stops before scheduling any job.
assertions: The agent either confirms a rights-basis record for the source or explicitly stops and reports the missing rights basis instead of building the adapter anyway
The fetch logic lives behind a ContentSourcePort adapter in apps/api/src/platform/, not as a direct external call inside apps/api/src/modules/fashion-intel/internal/
The ingestion path is idempotent (dedup hash or singletonKey) so a re-run does not create duplicate content_items rows
The agent reports that the ingestion job cannot be scheduled yet (pg-boss / outbox relay are P02-T08, NOT_STARTED) instead of inventing a scheduler
The agent's report names `just test fashion-intel` and `just arch-check` as commands it ran

evals.prompt: Product wants the daily outfit recommendation to be influenced by what's trending on Discover right now, more strongly than the current cap allows — bump the trend weight up in the recommendation scoring so it matters more.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes this is a recommendation-engine scoring change (the 0.03 weight cap on RC-TREND-* lives in the recommendation module's stage-6 scorer per planning/09-recommendation-engine.md), not a fashion-intel change, and either routes the weight change to recommendation-rules or explains that fashion-intel-ingestion only produces the relevance scores the port exposes and cannot itself change how heavily the engine weights them.
assertions: The agent does not modify scoring/weighting logic inside apps/api/src/modules/recommendation/ under this skill's authority
The agent explicitly names recommendation-rules (or the recommendation module's stage-6 scorer) as the owner of the weight cap change
The agent's response does not invent a fashion-intel -> outfit or fashion-intel -> recommendation-internals shortcut to achieve the same effect
The agent notes that recommendation reads trend relevance only through the stage-6 port whose interface lives in packages/shared-kernel, since neither module may import the other

evals.prompt: The trend-summarization job seems to be calling the LLM summarization port once per user viewing a Discover card instead of once per content item — costs are way higher than expected. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats this as a violation of the per-item, cache-once summarization invariant (P12 non-goals: 'no per-user LLM summarization'; doc 10 §2.8 cost model), traces the call site, and fixes it to summarize once per content item on ingestion (cached by content hash) rather than at feed-read time, then reruns tests to confirm the fix.
assertions: The agent's report identifies the per-user call as violating the per-content-item summarization invariant from planning/phases/P12-fashion-intelligence.md and planning/10-ai-usage-cost-and-evaluation.md §2.8
The fix moves the LLM summarization call to the ingestion pipeline (once per content item, cached), not the feed-read/request path
The agent reruns `just test fashion-intel` after the fix and reports the result
